chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The doer of good is better than the good itself, and the doer of evil is worse than the evil itself.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the good deed and the doer of good in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the moral weight of an action resides primarily in the agent rather than the act itself, a concept central to Shia ethical jurisprudence. This distinction elevates the status of the 'doer' (fa'il), suggesting that consistent character and intentionality define the true value of good or evil, surpassing the mere occurrence of the deed. It serves as a reminder that spiritual growth is measured by the transformation of the self, not just the accumulation of actions.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 32. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him,
said: The doer of good is better than the good itself, and the doer of evil is worse than the evil itself.
